proposals.title: Refresh the volunteer page from the Fall 2026 volunteer sheet
proposals.body:
## Summary

The user wants the /volunteer page brought in line with the "Fall 2026 | HIT Volunteer Opportunities" Google Sheet (Drive file 1YmLbinAVIhGYnJHKpy3B0aSpc7QpNoAZGggR0BcIJWc, tab "Fall 2026"). The sheet lists roles such as Alumni Volunteer Coordinator, City Volunteer and City Lead or Co-Lead (SF / Bay Area, Boston / Cambridge, NYC x AI Events), Founders Task Force volunteer and co-lead, and Editorial, each with a description and a point of contact. The site's volunteer projects live in the `projects` collection (`src/content/projects/*.md`) and render on /volunteer.

## Key Decisions

- Publish ROLES ONLY: title, description, and (if the user agrees) the point-of-contact name. Never publish the volunteer names, emails, phone numbers or availability columns the sheet also holds.
- One project entry per distinct role, not per "1 of ∞" row; the sheet repeats each role across rows.
- Confirm with the user which existing project entries (IG Content Creator, LinkedIn Engagement Specialist, Social Media Marketing Specialist, Writer) stay, merge, or retire.
- City lead/co-lead roles link naturally from the new "Lead or co-lead a chapter →" item in the Chapters menu, which already points at /volunteer.

## Implementation

1. Read the sheet's Fall 2026 tab and draft the role list for the user to confirm.
2. Add or update `src/content/projects/<role>.md` entries (title, blurb, active, dates, body), following the shape of `src/content/projects/ig-content-creator.md`.
3. Update the volunteer-page scenarios (`volunteer-page-open-projects`, `volunteer-page-no-open-projects`) and recapture after the content is committed.
proposals.reason: You asked for the volunteer opportunities to match your sheet; it was kept out of this change.

proposals.title: Seeded scenario captures break while site content is uncommitted
proposals.body:
## Summary

Scenario capture on this Astro site cannot produce trustworthy frames of SEEDED app scenarios while any file under `src/content/` or `src/data/` is uncommitted. The content sandbox (`initContentSandbox` in `astro.config.mjs`, `.codeyam/tmp/content-sandbox/`) does not engage, so seeds are refused ("served committed content"). The documented workaround of stashing those files for the capture pass also failed this session: it produced frames with the chapters and communities collections EMPTY (no Chapters menu group), and `recapture-stale` reported them as clean "Recaptured". Every content-changing feature therefore ends with seeded frames that must be restored by hand and force-recaptured after the commit.

## Key Decisions

- A capture whose seed or collections did not land must fail loudly, never report "Recaptured".
- The sandbox should seed from the WORKING TREE's `src/content` when it is dirty, rather than switching off, so content edits and seeded scenarios can be captured together before the commit.

## Implementation

1. In `astro.config.mjs` (`initContentSandbox`), seed the sandbox from the working-tree `src/content`/`src/data` when dirty, and never leave a collection directory empty across a dev-server restart (the empty-collection-dir watcher bug).
2. Add a post-capture assertion for seeded app scenarios: when a collection the page renders is empty but the seed or production content has rows, fail the capture.
3. Re-verify with `harvard-in-tech-phone-menu-open` and `webinars-route-the-surviving-recordings`, which both captured empty roster frames this session.
proposals.reason: Seeded full-page screenshots came out empty or wrong but were reported as captured.

proposals.title: Point the homepage newsletter card at the Mailchimp sign-up
proposals.body:
## Summary

On 2026-10-09 the owner asked for the menu's Newsletter link to go to the Mailchimp sign-up rather than the LinkedIn newsletter, and the menu now does. The homepage Content Hub section still offers a "LinkedIn newsletter" card pointing at linkedin.com/newsletters/..., and the welcome blog post links there too, so the site sends people to two different newsletters depending on where they click.

## Key Decisions

- Use the one sign-up URL the site already treats as canonical: `links.mailingList` in `src/data/settings.json`, read through `siteLinks()` in `src/lib/site.ts`. Do not hard-code the URL again.
- Rename the card to plain "Newsletter" with a blurb about email, since it will no longer be a LinkedIn feed item.
- Decide with the owner whether the LinkedIn newsletter is kept anywhere at all (for example under the LinkedIn company page) or dropped.

## Implementation

- `src/components/landing/ContentHub.astro` line 54: replace the LinkedIn newsletter entry's label, blurb and url (via `siteLinks().mailingList`). Check the brand-icon pick in `src/lib/brandIcons.ts`, which matches on the label text.
- `src/content/blog/welcome.md` line 19: update or remove the LinkedIn newsletter link.
- Recapture the Content Hub component scenarios and the homepage scenarios.
proposals.reason: The menu's Newsletter now goes to Mailchimp, but the homepage Content Hub card still says LinkedIn newsletter.

proposals.title: Screenshot staleness misses data files the page reads at runtime
proposals.body:
## What happened

This feature changed only `src/data/nav.json` (plus a few code files). The site reads that file at runtime through `readSingleton('nav.json')` in `src/lib/site.ts`, not through an import, so the screenshot staleness hash never includes it. Two seeded /donate scenarios were captured with the old menu while nav.json was stashed (the stash was needed to get the seeded captures past the dirty-content guard), and afterwards `scenario-coverage`, the strict audit and `session-finalize` Phase 3.5 all reported them as fresh. The only way to find them was to eyeball the header of each frame, and fixing them needed `recapture-stale --force --target`.

## What would have helped

Include content/data files that pages read at runtime (`src/data/*.json`, `src/content/**`) in the render-input hash, at least for application scenarios on this stack, or let `stack.json` declare runtime-read data roots. A frame that shows stale data should read as stale.
proposals.reason: Frames showing the old menu were reported fresh because nav.json is not part of the staleness hash.

proposals.title: Syncing capture scripts marks every screenshot stale
proposals.body:
## What happened

At Verify Prototype, `client-errors` refused to run because `.codeyam/capture.js` predated the binary and said to run `sync-capture-scripts`. After the sync, `scenario-coverage` reported 229 of 293 scenarios stale with reason "capture pipeline changed". The full `recapture-stale` sweep took about 38 minutes, and 247 of its captures came back pixel-identical and were restored. None of that work was related to the feature.

## What would have helped

Treat a capture-script sync as a re-verify rather than a staleness event, or let the sync record the new pipeline version without invalidating frames until a capture actually differs. At minimum, have `client-errors` and `sync-capture-scripts` warn up front that the sync makes the whole corpus stale and roughly how long the sweep will take.
proposals.reason: One required script sync turned 229 untouched scenarios stale and cost a long full sweep that changed nothing.

proposals.title: Frame the past-events section in the two events-page scenarios
proposals.body:
## Summary

The scenarios `events-route-the-calendar-with-no-past-events-yet` and `events-route-upcoming-and-past` seed different event sets, but both capture only the top of `/events` (page banner plus the Luma calendar embed). The past-events listing where they differ sits below the visible area, so the two frames are byte-identical and `scenario-review` flags the pair as a seed-error candidate. Before this was noticed they only differed by whatever the live Luma widget happened to show.

## Key Decisions

- Add an `interactions` hover on the past-events heading to each scenario, so each capture frames the section that proves its state (URL fragments do not scroll captures).
- Do not mock or freeze the Luma embed here; framing past the embed avoids depending on its live content.

## Implementation

- `.codeyam/scenarios/events-route-the-calendar-with-no-past-events-yet.json` and `.codeyam/scenarios/events-route-upcoming-and-past.json`: add `"interactions": [{"action": "hover", "text": "<past events heading>"}]`, reading the heading from `src/components/EventsPage.astro`.
- Recapture both with `--force --target` and confirm the frames now differ.
proposals.reason: The 'no past events yet' and 'upcoming and past' events-page screenshots are identical, because the part that differs is below the visible area.

proposals.title: Dev server stop and start leaves a second astro dev running
proposals.body:
## What happened

Two `astro dev` processes ran all session (one on :4322 owned by the editor, a stray on :4323). The only hint was a one-line `app realigned to :4323` note on an early `preview`. A full `recapture-stale` then wrote 49 frames while the two servers raced on `.astro/data-store.json`; some captured the UnknownFilesystemError page and others captured production content instead of the seed, yet most were reported as Recaptured. `dev-server stop` left the stray alive, and a following `dev-server start` re-created the pair (supervisor respawn plus the start). Recovery meant finding the stray by hand through `/proc` socket inodes (no `ss` or `lsof` in the container), killing it by PID, discarding all 49 frames and recapturing.

## What would have helped

`recapture-stale` and `register` refusing to capture while more than one `astro dev` is alive, naming the stray PID and port. `dev-server stop` and `restart` guaranteeing exactly one process afterwards, and `dev-server` status reporting the count. Treating a port realignment as an error, not a note.
proposals.reason: Two dev servers silently corrupted a full recapture: frames came out as an Astro error page or with the wrong content.

proposals.title: scenario-review counts seed-error candidates without naming them
proposals.body:
## What happened

`scenario-review --target /` ended with `2 seed-error candidate(s)` while every row it printed was `[ok]`. Its suggested follow-up, `seeded-capture-check`, only checks native device seeds and reported OK. Finding the pair took an md5 sweep over `.codeyam/scenarios/screenshots/`.

## What would have helped

Print the flagged slug pairs next to the count, and make `seeded-capture-check` cover web scenarios with a content seed, or stop recommending it for them.
proposals.reason: The review said '2 seed-error candidates' but listed every scenario as ok, so the pair had to be found by hashing screenshots by hand.

proposals.title: preview-flow has no way to scroll the page
proposals.body:
## What happened

To demo a header that changes once the page scrolls, `preview-flow` offered navigate, click, press, fill, waitFor and capture, but no scroll. Pressing PageDown on `body` did not scroll the capture browser, so the `waitFor` timed out and no frames were kept. The workaround was clicking an inert heading lower on the page, relying on Playwright scrolling it into view.

## What would have helped

A `scroll` step (`{"scroll": 1200}` or `{"scroll": {"selector": "..."}}`), and the same for scenario `interactions`, where `hover` currently stands in for it.
proposals.reason: Demoing a scroll-dependent feature took a failed PageDown attempt and a click-a-heading workaround.

proposals.title: Content edits stay invisible in the preview until the sandbox copy is replaced by hand
proposals.body:
## What happened

Adding `src/content/homeSections/mission.md`, and later editing its title, did not reach the live preview: the dev server reads `.codeyam/tmp/content-sandbox/`, restored from the `content-sandbox-active` snapshot, which kept the older copy. The first time took deleting the snapshot and restarting the dev server (each restart also left a stray `astro dev` behind); the second took copying the file into both sandbox folders by hand. Meanwhile the user, looking at the preview pane, reported twice that the change was not there.

## What would have helped

The sandbox picking up edits to committed `src/content`/`src/data` files for entries the active scenario does not seed, or a `content-sync` command that refreshes the sandbox and snapshot from the working tree without a restart. Also a preview-pane notice when the pane is parked on a scenario whose seed shadows the file just edited.
proposals.reason: A new content entry and a reworded heading did not show in the preview until the sandbox copies were overwritten by hand.

proposals.title: Give the chapter Sign up band a benefit-led pitch
proposals.body:
## Summary

Every chapter page carries two newsletter pitches. The global-community band's card now leads with what lands in the inbox ("Get the newsletter" — events, chapter news and alumni stories, local news first). The chapter's own "Stay in touch / Sign up" band (`src/components/ChapterSignUp.astro`) still reads "Join the Harvard Alumni in Tech community." with a bare "Subscribe" button, which says nothing about what a reader gets and repeats the ask without a reason. Rewrite that band so it pitches the chapter-local benefit — hearing about this city's events first — and so the two pitches on one page complement rather than echo each other.

## Key Decisions

- Keep the band and its Mailchimp link (`siteLinks().mailingList`, overridable via `subscribeUrl`); change wording only.
- Make it chapter-specific where possible (e.g. pass the city name so the intro can say "Hear about London events first"), since the global-community card already covers the general pitch.
- Do not add a subscriber count; that figure is hard-coded in several places already and drifts.
- Leave the header "Subscribe" button alone — it must stay one short word at 390px.

## Implementation

### 1. Rewrite the band copy

**File**: `src/components/ChapterSignUp.astro` (45 lines)

Update the `SectionHead` `kicker` / `title` / `intro` and the button label. If the copy names the city, add an optional `city` prop and pass it from `src/components/ChapterPage.astro`.

### 2. Keep fixtures and scenarios in step

Update `src/pages/isolated-components/ChapterSignUp.astro` and recapture the `ChapterSignUp - Default` scenario plus the chapter-page scenarios that show the band.
proposals.reason: Chapter pages now pitch the newsletter twice: the new benefit-led card, and a generic 'Sign up / Subscribe' band above it.
